questions.text: दो बिन्दु आवेश Q और –q मुक्त आकाश में एक-दूसरे से 'r' दूरी पर स्थित हैं। इन दोनों आवेशों को मिलाने वाली रेखा के लम्बवत प्रदेश में कोई एकसमान विद्युत-क्षेत्र E सदिश अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है। आवेश –q पर कार्यरत नेट बल की दिशा और Q और –q को मिलाने वाली रेखा के बीच कोण क्या होगा?
questions.text_english: Two point charges Q and -q are held 'r' distance apart in free space. A uniform electric field E (vector) is applied in the region perpendicular to the line joining the two charges. Which one of the following angles will the direction of the net force acting on charge -q make with the line joining Q and -q?
questions.solution: The force on charge -q due to charge Q is the Coulomb attractive force F_C = KQq/r² directed along the line joining the two charges (toward Q). The applied electric field E acts perpendicular to this line on -q, giving a force F_E = qE perpendicular to the line. The angle θ that the net force makes with the line joining Q and -q is given by tan θ = F_E/F_C = qE/(KQq/r²) = 4πε₀Er²/Q. Therefore θ = tan⁻¹(4πε₀Er²/Q), which is option (A). Options (B) and (D) use cot⁻¹ which gives the complement of the correct angle, and option (C) has the ratio inverted.

questions.text: समान पदार्थ के तीन तारों A, B और C की लम्बाइयाँ और अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल क्रमश: (2l, A/2), (l, A) तथा (l/2, 2A) हैं। यदि इन तारों के प्रतिरोध क्रमश: R_A, R_B और R_C हैं, तो:
questions.text_english: Three wires A, B and C of the same material have lengths and area of cross-sections as (2l, A/2), (l, A) and (l/2, 2A), respectively. If the resistances of these wires are R_A, R_B and R_C respectively, then:
questions.solution: Using the formula R = ρl/A, where ρ is the same for all three wires: R_A = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A; R_B = ρl/A; R_C = ρ(l/2)/(2A) = ρl/4A. Comparing: R_A = 4ρl/A, R_C = ρl/4A = 0.25ρl/A, R_B = ρl/A. So R_A > R_B > R_C. Wait — let me recheck: R_A = 4ρl/A, R_B = ρl/A = 1ρl/A, R_C = 0.25ρl/A. Therefore R_A > R_B > R_C, which is option (A). Option (A) is correct.

questions.text: द्रव्यमान m और आवेश q का कोई कण y-अक्ष के अनुदिश किसी ऐसे प्रदेश में गतिमान है जिसमें x-अक्ष के अनुदिश कोई एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B सदिश कार्यरत है। इस आवेश पर कार्यरत लॉरेन्ज बल किस दिशा के अनुदिश होगा?
questions.text_english: A particle of mass m and charge q moves along y-axis in a region in which a uniform magnetic field B (vector) is pointing along x-axis. The Lorentz force acting on the charge will point along:
questions.solution: The Lorentz force is given by F = q(v × B). Here velocity v = v ĵ (along y-axis) and B = B î (along x-axis). So F = q(v ĵ × B î) = qvB(ĵ × î) = qvB(-k̂) = -qvB k̂. For positive charge q, the force points along the negative z-axis. Option (D) is correct. Option (C) would be correct for a negative charge. Options (A) and (B) are wrong because the cross product of y and x vectors gives a z-direction result, not x or y.

questions.text: कोई छड़ चुम्बक आरम्भ में किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र से समकोण बनाता है। इस चुम्बक को तब तक घूर्णित किया जाता है जब तक कि इस पर कार्यरत बल-आघूर्ण उसके आरम्भिक मान का आधा हो जाए। छड़ चुम्बक को जिस कोण तक घूर्णित किया गया है, वह है:
questions.text_english: A bar magnet is initially at right angles to a uniform magnetic field. The magnet is rotated till the torque acting on it becomes one-half of its initial value. The angle through which the bar magnet is rotated is:
questions.solution: The torque on a bar magnet in a uniform field is τ = MB sinθ, where θ is the angle between the magnetic moment and the field. Initially the magnet is at 90° to the field, so τ_initial = MB sin90° = MB. After rotation by angle φ, the new angle with the field is (90° - φ), and τ_new = MB sin(90° - φ) = MB cosφ. Setting τ_new = τ_initial/2: MB cosφ = MB/2, so cosφ = 1/2, giving φ = 60°. Option (C) is correct.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस पदार्थ की चुम्बकशीलता मुक्त आकाश की चुम्बकशीलता से कम है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following substances has magnetic permeability less than that of free space?
questions.solution: Substances with magnetic permeability less than that of free space (μ₀) are called diamagnetic materials. Diamagnetic materials are repelled by magnetic fields and have relative permeability μᵣ slightly less than 1. Copper is a diamagnetic material (μᵣ < 1), so its permeability is less than μ₀. Sodium and Aluminium are paramagnetic (μᵣ slightly > 1), and Iron is strongly ferromagnetic (μᵣ >> 1). Therefore option (D) Copper is correct.

questions.text: किसी बन्द कुण्डली से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स (Wb में) समय t (s में) के साथ φ = 5t² + 4t – 2 की भाँति विचरण करता है। यदि परिपथ का प्रतिरोध 14 Ω है, तो t = 1 s पर कुण्डली में प्रेरित धारा का परिमाण होगा:
questions.text_english: The magnetic flux linked with a closed coil (in Wb) varies with time t (in s) as φ = 5t² + 4t – 2. If the resistance of the circuit is 14 Ω, the magnitude of induced current in the coil at t = 1 s will be:
questions.solution: The induced emf is ε = -dφ/dt. Differentiating φ = 5t² + 4t – 2 with respect to t: dφ/dt = 10t + 4. At t = 1 s: dφ/dt = 10(1) + 4 = 14 V. The magnitude of induced emf |ε| = 14 V. The induced current I = |ε|/R = 14/14 = 1·0 A. Option (B) is correct. The other options arise from incorrect differentiation or substitution errors.

questions.text: मुक्त आकाश में गतिमान किसी विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग के चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र का आयाम 6·0 × 10⁻⁴ T है। इसके विद्युत-क्षेत्र का आयाम है:
questions.text_english: In an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space, the amplitude of magnetic field is 6·0 × 10⁻⁴ T. The amplitude of its electric field is:
questions.solution: For an electromagnetic wave in free space, the ratio of electric field amplitude to magnetic field amplitude equals the speed of light: E₀/B₀ = c. Therefore E₀ = B₀ × c = 6·0 × 10⁻⁴ × 3 × 10⁸ = 18 × 10⁴ = 1·8 × 10⁵ Vm⁻¹. Option (C) is correct. Option (A) would result from dividing instead of multiplying by c; option (B) arises from an error of order of magnitude; option (D) is incorrect multiplication.

questions.text: ऊर्ध्वाधरत: रखे किसी लम्बे सीधे तार से ऊपर की ओर कोई स्थायी धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस धारावाही तार द्वारा उत्पन्न चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं की आकृति है:
questions.text_english: A long straight wire is held vertically and carries a steady current in upward direction. The shape of magnetic field lines produced by the current-carrying wire are:

options.A: horizontal straight lines directed radially out from the wire.
options.B: straight lines parallel to the current-carrying wire.
options.C: concentric horizontal circles around the wire.

options_english.A: horizontal straight lines directed radially out from the wire.
options_english.B: straight lines parallel to the current-carrying wire.
options_english.C: concentric horizontal circles around the wire.

questions.solution: By the right-hand thumb rule (or Ampere's circuital law), the magnetic field lines produced by a long straight current-carrying wire form concentric circles in planes perpendicular to the wire. Since the wire is vertical, these planes are horizontal, so the field lines are concentric horizontal circles centred on the wire. Option (C) is correct. Options (A) and (B) are wrong shapes for magnetic field lines around a straight wire; option (D) describes helical paths which would be produced by a combination of fields.
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Straight Wire

questions.text: किसी गोलीय दर्पण द्वारा उत्पन्न आवर्धन –2·0 है। उपयोग किए गए दर्पण तथा बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति होगी:
questions.text_english: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is –2·0. The mirror used and the nature of the image formed will be:
questions.solution: The magnification m = -v/u = -2·0. A negative magnification means the image is inverted and real. A convex mirror always produces virtual, erect, and diminished images (m is always positive and less than 1 for convex mirrors). A magnification of -2 (greater than 1 in magnitude and negative) means the image is enlarged, inverted, and real, which is only possible with a concave mirror when the object is placed between f and 2f. Therefore the mirror is concave and the image is real. Option (B) is correct.

questions.text: सही कथन चुनिए:
questions.text_english: Choose the correct statement:

options.A: प्रकाश के फ़ोटॉन विवर्तन दर्शाते हैं जबकि इलेक्ट्रॉन विवर्तन नहीं दर्शाते हैं।
options.B: इलेक्ट्रॉनों में संवेग होता है जबकि फ़ोटॉनों में संवेग नहीं होता है।
options.C: प्रकाश के फ़ोटॉन तथा इलेक्ट्रॉन दोनों ही द्वैत प्रकृति दर्शाते हैं।
options.D: सभी विद्युत-चुम्बकीय विकिरणों में फ़ोटॉन नहीं होते हैं।

options_english.A: Photons of light show diffraction whereas electrons do not show diffraction.
options_english.B: Electrons have momentum whereas photons do not have momentum.
options_english.C: Photons of light and electrons both exhibit dual nature.
options_english.D: All electromagnetic radiations do not have photons.

questions.solution: Both photons and electrons exhibit wave-particle duality. Photons, being electromagnetic quanta, show both wave properties (like diffraction and interference) and particle properties (like the photoelectric effect). Electrons similarly show particle behaviour in normal collisions and wave behaviour (de Broglie waves), confirmed by Davisson-Germer diffraction experiments. Option (A) is false because electrons do show diffraction. Option (B) is false because photons carry momentum p = h/λ. Option (D) is false because all electromagnetic radiations are composed of photons. Option (C) is the correct statement.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: किसी लाल प्रकाश पुन्ज और किसी नीले प्रकाश पुन्ज की तीव्रताएँ समान हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?
questions.text_english: A beam of red light and a beam of blue light have equal intensities. Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The blue beam has more number of photons than the red beam.
options.B: The red beam has more number of photons than the blue beam.
options.C: Wavelength of red light is lesser than wavelength of blue light.
options.D: The blue light beam has lesser energy per photon than that in the red light beam.

options_english.A: The blue beam has more number of photons than the red beam.
options_english.B: The red beam has more number of photons than the blue beam.
options_english.C: Wavelength of red light is lesser than wavelength of blue light.
options_english.D: The blue light beam has lesser energy per photon than that in the red light beam.

questions.solution: Energy per photon E = hf = hc/λ. Since blue light has a shorter wavelength (higher frequency) than red light, each blue photon carries more energy than each red photon. Since both beams have equal intensity (same total energy per unit time per unit area), and red photons have less energy individually, the red beam must contain more photons to carry the same total energy. Therefore option (B) is correct. Option (C) is false because red light has a longer wavelength than blue. Option (D) is false because blue photons have higher energy.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कक्ष ताप पर विद्युत चालक है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is an electrical conductor at room temperature?
questions.solution: Tin (Sn) is a metal and is an electrical conductor at room temperature. Mica is an insulator used in electrical equipment precisely because it does not conduct electricity. Silicon (Si) is a semiconductor, which has very high resistivity at room temperature compared to metals. Carbon (C) in its diamond form is an insulator (graphite conducts but the question likely refers to diamond allotrope in this context). Tin (Sn) is therefore the correct conductor. Option (A) is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): द्विझिरी प्रयोग में यदि एक झिरी बन्द है, तो परदे पर अन्य झिरी के कारण विवर्तन पैटर्न दृष्टिगोचर होगा।
कारण (R): व्यतिकरण के लिए कम-से-कम दो तरंगों की आवश्यकता होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In double slit experiment if one slit is closed, diffraction pattern due to the other slit will appear on the screen.
Reason (R): For interference, at least two waves are required.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रकार के प्रश्न हैं।
questions.instruction_line_english: Questions number 13 to 16 are Assertion (A) and Reason (R) type questions. Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: when one slit is closed in a double slit experiment, only a single slit remains, and light passing through it produces a diffraction pattern on the screen (a broad central maximum with alternating bright and dark fringes). The Reason is also true: interference does indeed require at least two coherent waves. However, the Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion. The diffraction pattern in the Assertion arises from a single slit, which is a single-slit diffraction phenomenon, not interference between two waves. Hence both statements are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Option (B) is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): किसी एकवर्णी आपतित विकिरण के लिए, किसी दी गई धातु से उत्सर्जित फ़ोटोइलेक्ट्रॉनों की चाल शून्य से किसी निश्चित अधिकतम मान तक के परास में होती है।
कारण (R): प्रत्येक धातु का अपना निश्चित कार्यफलन होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): For monochromatic incident radiation, the emitted photoelectrons from a given metal have speed ranging from zero to a certain maximum value.
Reason (R): Each metal has a definite work function.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: photoelectrons emitted under monochromatic radiation have a range of speeds from zero to a certain maximum. This happens because electrons at different energy levels within the metal need different amounts of energy to escape the surface; those deeper inside lose more energy to collisions. The Reason is also true: each metal has a definite work function (minimum energy needed to eject an electron from the surface). However, the Reason (work function being a fixed value) explains the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, not the range of speeds. The range arises from electrons originating at different depths. Hence both are true but Reason does not correctly explain Assertion. Option (B) is correct.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक ऋणावेशित नहीं होता है।
कारण (R): नैज अर्धचालक (उदासीन) में मादित उदासीन पंचसंयोजक अपद्रव्य परमाणु क्रिस्टल जालक को अपना पाँचवाँ अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन दान करके धनात्मक दाता बन जाता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): n-type semiconductor is not negatively charged.
Reason (R): Neutral pentavalent impurity atom doped in intrinsic semiconductor (neutral) donates its fifth unpaired electron to the crystal lattice and becomes a positive donor.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: an n-type semiconductor is electrically neutral overall. Although it has an excess of free electrons (majority carriers), the donor atoms that contributed these electrons are now positively ionised fixed ions. The total positive charge of donor ions exactly balances the total negative charge of free electrons, so the semiconductor is neutral. The Reason is also true: when a neutral pentavalent impurity (like phosphorus) is doped into the lattice, it donates its fifth electron to the lattice and becomes a positive ion (donor). This correctly explains why the semiconductor remains neutral despite having extra electrons. Therefore both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason correctly explains Assertion. Option (A) is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): अनुनाद पर कोई श्रेणी LCR परिपथ शुद्ध प्रतिरोधी परिपथ की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
कारण (R): अनुनाद पर, X_L = X_C से ω = 1/√(LC) प्राप्त होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): A series LCR circuit behaves as a pure resistive circuit at resonance.
Reason (R): At resonance, X_L = X_C gives ω = 1/√(LC).

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: at resonance in a series LCR circuit, the inductive reactance X_L exactly cancels the capacitive reactance X_C, so the net reactance is zero. The impedance Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²) = R, and the circuit behaves as a pure resistor. The Reason is also true: at resonance X_L = X_C means ωL = 1/ωC, which gives ω = 1/√(LC), the resonant angular frequency. Furthermore, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion because when X_L = X_C, their effects cancel making the circuit purely resistive. Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason correctly explains Assertion. Option (A) is correct.

questions.text: किसी नैज अर्धचालक में, वाहक सांद्रता 5 × 10⁸ m⁻³ है। अपद्रव्यी परमाणुओं द्वारा मादित करने पर विवर सांद्रता 8 × 10¹² m⁻³ हो जाती है। (क) (i) डोपक (मादक) के प्रकार को पहचानिए तथा (ii) इस प्रकार बने अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक को पहचानिए। (ख) अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक में इलेक्ट्रॉन सांद्रता परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In an intrinsic semiconductor, carrier's concentration is 5 × 10⁸ m⁻³. On doping with impurity atoms, the hole concentration becomes 8 × 10¹² m⁻³. (a) Identify (i) the type of dopant and (ii) the extrinsic semiconductor so formed. (b) Calculate the electron concentration in the extrinsic semiconductor.

key_points: Hole concentration increased beyond intrinsic concentration → p-type semiconductor formed by doping with trivalent (acceptor) impurity
Dopant is a trivalent element (e.g. Boron, Aluminium) — p-type semiconductor

questions.solution: (a) Since the hole concentration (8 × 10¹² m⁻³) is much greater than the intrinsic carrier concentration (5 × 10⁸ m⁻³), holes are the majority carriers. This means a trivalent (acceptor) impurity such as Boron or Aluminium was used as the dopant. The extrinsic semiconductor formed is a p-type semiconductor. (b) Using the mass action law: n_e × n_h = n_i². Therefore, n_e = n_i²/n_h = (5 × 10⁸)² / (8 × 10¹²) = 25 × 10¹⁶ / 8 × 10¹² = 3.125 × 10⁴ m⁻³. The electron concentration in the extrinsic semiconductor is 3.125 × 10⁴ m⁻³.

questions.text: यंग के द्विझिरी प्रयोग में परदे को झिरियों की ओर 30 cm विस्थापित किया गया है। इसके फलस्वरूप, फ्रिंज की चौड़ाई में 0·09 mm का परिवर्तन हो जाता है। यदि प्रयुक्त झिरी पृथकन 2 mm है, तो इस प्रयोग में प्रयुक्त प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In Young's double slit experiment, the screen is moved 30 cm towards the slits. As a consequence, the fringe width of the pattern changes by 0·09 mm. If the slits separation used is 2 mm, calculate the wavelength of light used in the experiment.

key_points: Fringe width β = λD/d; change Δβ = λΔD/d

questions.solution: The fringe width in Young's double slit experiment is given by β = λD/d, where λ is the wavelength, D is the distance from slits to screen, and d is the slit separation. When the screen is moved closer by ΔD = 30 cm = 0·30 m, the change in fringe width is Δβ = λΔD/d. Rearranging, λ = Δβ × d / ΔD = (0·09 × 10⁻³ m × 2 × 10⁻³ m) / (0·30 m) = (0·18 × 10⁻⁶) / 0·30 = 6 × 10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm. The wavelength of light used is 600 nm.

questions.text: किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस के दोनों पृष्ठों की वक्रता त्रिज्या 'R' है। वह शर्त प्राप्त कीजिए जिसमें इस लेंस की फोकस दूरी 'f' का मान 'R' के बराबर होगा। यदि इस लेंस का कोई एक पृष्ठ समतल कर दिया जाए, तो इस लेंस की नई फोकस दूरी क्या होगी?
questions.text_english: The two surfaces of a biconvex lens are of radius of curvature 'R' each. Obtain the condition under which its focal length 'f' be equal to 'R'. If one of the two surfaces of this lens is made plane, what will be the new focal length of the lens?

key_points: Using Lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n-1)[1/R₁ - 1/R₂]. For biconvex: R₁ = R, R₂ = -R, so 1/f = (n-1)(2/R). For f = R: 1/R = (n-1)(2/R) → n = 1.5
Condition: refractive index n = 1.5
If one surface is made plane (R₂ → ∞): 1/f_new = (n-1)(1/R) = (1.5-1)(1/R) = 0.5/R → f_new = 2R

questions.solution: For a biconvex lens with both surfaces of radius R, the lensmaker's equation gives 1/f = (n - 1)[1/R₁ - 1/R₂]. Taking R₁ = +R and R₂ = -R (sign convention for biconvex lens): 1/f = (n - 1)(1/R + 1/R) = 2(n - 1)/R. For f = R: 1/R = 2(n - 1)/R, which gives n - 1 = 1/2, so n = 1·5. The condition is that the refractive index of the lens material must be 1·5. If one surface is made plane (say R₂ → ∞), then 1/f_new = (n - 1)(1/R) = (0·5)(1/R). Therefore f_new = 2R.

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में, जब कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन n = 3 की अवस्था से n = 2 की अवस्था में संक्रमण करता है, तो कक्षा की त्रिज्या में प्रतिशत परिवर्तन ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In Bohr's model of hydrogen atom, find the percentage change in the radius of its orbit when an electron makes a transition from n = 3 state to n = 2 state.

key_points: r_n = n²a₀ (Bohr radius proportional to n²)
r₃ = 9a₀, r₂ = 4a₀
Percentage change = (r₂ - r₃)/r₃ × 100 = (4a₀ - 9a₀)/9a₀ × 100 = -55.6%

questions.solution: In Bohr's model, the radius of the nth orbit is r_n = n²a₀, where a₀ is the Bohr radius (0·53 Å). For n = 3: r₃ = 9a₀. For n = 2: r₂ = 4a₀. The percentage change in radius when the electron transitions from n = 3 to n = 2 is: Percentage change = (r₂ - r₃)/r₃ × 100 = (4a₀ - 9a₀)/9a₀ × 100 = (-5/9) × 100 = -55·6%. The radius decreases by approximately 55·6%.

questions.text: (क) दिए गए आरेख में तीन सर्वसम बल्ब P, Q और S किसी बैटरी से संयोजित हैं। (i) कुंजी K बन्द होने पर बल्ब P और Q की चमक की तुलना बल्ब S की चमक से कीजिए। (ii) जब कुंजी K खुली है तब बल्ब S और Q की चमक की तुलना कीजिए। दोनों प्रकरणों में अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) In the given figure, three identical bulbs P, Q and S are connected to a battery. (i) Compare the brightness of bulbs P and Q with that of bulb S when key K is closed. (ii) Compare the brightness of the bulbs S and Q when the key K is opened. Justify your answer in both cases.

key_points: When K is closed: P and Q are in series (forming one branch), S is in parallel with PQ series combination. P and Q share voltage, so they glow less brightly than S.
When K is open: P is disconnected (no current through P), so only Q and S are in series and both glow equally (same current through both).

questions.solution: (i) When key K is closed: Bulbs P and Q are in series with each other, and this series combination is connected in parallel with bulb S. Since P and Q share the total voltage, each receives only half the voltage across S. Therefore P and Q glow less brightly than S. (ii) When key K is opened: No current flows through P (the circuit through P is broken). Bulbs S and Q are now effectively in series with the battery. Both carry the same current and since they are identical, they glow equally brightly.

questions.text: (क) p-प्रकार तथा n-प्रकार के अर्धचालकों में बहुसंख्यक और अल्पसंख्यक आवेश वाहक क्या होते हैं? (ख) किसी p-n संधि डायोड में विसरण धारा और अपवाह धारा निर्मित होने की संक्षेप में व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) What are majority and minority charge carriers of p-type and n-type semiconductors? (b) Explain briefly the formation of diffusion current and drift current in a p-n junction diode.

key_points: p-type: majority carriers = holes, minority carriers = electrons; n-type: majority carriers = electrons, minority carriers = holes
Diffusion current: due to concentration gradient, holes diffuse from p to n side and electrons from n to p side, creating a diffusion current from p to n
Drift current: the built-in electric field in the depletion region drives minority carriers (electrons from p-side, holes from n-side) across the junction, forming drift current from n to p

questions.solution: (a) In a p-type semiconductor, holes are the majority charge carriers and electrons are the minority carriers. In an n-type semiconductor, electrons are the majority charge carriers and holes are the minority carriers. (b) When a p-n junction is formed, holes from the p-side and electrons from the n-side diffuse across the junction due to the concentration gradient. This movement of charge constitutes the diffusion current, which flows from the p-side to the n-side. As diffusion proceeds, the uncovered donor and acceptor ions near the junction form a depletion layer with an internal electric field pointing from n to p. This field opposes further diffusion but drives the minority carriers (electrons from p-side, holes from n-side) across the junction, forming the drift current in the direction from n to p. At equilibrium, the diffusion current equals the drift current and the net current is zero.

questions.text: (क) किन प्रकरणों में कोई आवेशित कण किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में किसी बल का अनुभव नहीं करता है? (ख) आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार, भुजा 'l' का कोई वर्गाकार पाश MNPK जिससे कोई धारा 'I₂' प्रवाहित हो रही है किसी लम्बे सीधे तार, जिससे कोई स्थायी धारा 'I₁' प्रवाहित हो रही है, के निकट उसी के ही तल में स्थित है। तार द्वारा पाश पर आरोपित चुम्बकीय बल का परिमाण प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) In which cases does a charged particle not experience a force in a magnetic field? (b) A square loop MNPK of side 'l' carrying a current 'I₂' is kept close to a long straight wire in the same plane and the wire carries a steady current I₁ as shown in the figure. Obtain the magnitude of magnetic force exerted by the wire on the loop.

key_points: A charged particle does not experience force if: (i) it is stationary (v = 0), or (ii) it moves parallel or antiparallel to the magnetic field (θ = 0° or 180°)
The MN side (closer to wire at distance l from wire) and KP side (at distance 2l from wire) experience forces; MK and NP sides are parallel to wire so forces cancel
Net force = F_MN - F_KP = (μ₀I₁I₂l)/(2πl) - (μ₀I₁I₂l)/(2π(2l)) = μ₀I₁I₂/(2π) - μ₀I₁I₂/(4π) = μ₀I₁I₂/(4π), directed toward the wire

questions.solution: (a) A charged particle does not experience a magnetic force in two cases: (i) when the particle is at rest (since F = qv × B = 0 if v = 0), and (ii) when the particle moves parallel or antiparallel to the direction of the magnetic field (since the angle θ between v and B is 0° or 180°, making sinθ = 0 and F = qvB sinθ = 0). (b) The two sides MN and KP are parallel to the current-carrying wire and carry forces. The sides MK and NP are perpendicular to the wire but equal and opposite, so they cancel. The force on side MN (at distance l from wire): F_MN = μ₀I₁I₂l/(2πl) = μ₀I₁I₂/(2π), directed toward the wire. The force on side KP (at distance 2l from wire): F_KP = μ₀I₁I₂l/(2π × 2l) = μ₀I₁I₂/(4π), directed away from the wire. The net force on the loop = F_MN - F_KP = μ₀I₁I₂/(2π) - μ₀I₁I₂/(4π) = μ₀I₁I₂/(4π), directed toward the wire.
questions.topic: Force on a Current Loop near a Wire

questions.text: (क) लम्बाई 'l', अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल 'A' तथा फेरों की संख्या 'N' की किसी लम्बी परिनालिका के स्व-प्रेरकत्व के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए। (ख) आरेख में दो कुण्डलियों '1' और '2' में धारा में परिवर्तन की दर और प्रेरित वि.वा. बल (emf) (ε) के परिमाण के बीच ग्राफ दर्शाए गए हैं। इनमें से किस कुण्डली के स्व-प्रेरकत्व का मान अधिक है और क्यों?
questions.text_english: (a) Obtain an expression for the self-inductance of a long solenoid of length 'l', cross-sectional area 'A' and having 'N' turns. (b) The figure shows the plot of magnitude of induced emf (ε) versus the rate of change of current in two coils '1' and '2'. Which coil has greater value of self-inductance and why?

key_points: B = μ₀nI = μ₀(N/l)I; Total flux linkage NΦ = N × BA = μ₀N²AI/l; L = NΦ/I = μ₀N²A/l
From the graph, coil 1 has a steeper slope than coil 2
Since ε = L(dI/dt), slope of ε vs dI/dt graph = L; coil 1 with greater slope has greater self-inductance

questions.solution: (a) For a long solenoid of length l, cross-sectional area A, and N turns, the number of turns per unit length is n = N/l. The magnetic field inside is B = μ₀nI = μ₀NI/l. The total magnetic flux linkage is NΦ = N × BA = μ₀N²AI/l. The self-inductance is L = NΦ/I = μ₀N²A/l. (b) The induced emf is given by ε = L(dI/dt). On the plot of |ε| versus dI/dt, the slope of each line equals the self-inductance L. From the figure, coil 1 has a steeper slope than coil 2. Therefore, coil 1 has a greater value of self-inductance.

questions.text: आइंस्टाइन के प्रकाश-विद्युत समीकरण का उपयोग करते हुए निम्नलिखित प्रेक्षणों की व्याख्या कीजिए: (क) जब किसी पृष्ठ पर आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति किसी निश्चित निम्नतम मान से कम होती है तो प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन नहीं होता है। (ख) आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति न कि आपतित प्रकाश की तीव्रता फ़ोटोइलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा को प्रभावित करती है। (ग) आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति (ν) और अंतक वोल्टता (V₀) के बीच वक्र एक सरल रेखा होती है, जिसकी ढाल (प्रवणता) h/e होती है।
questions.text_english: Explain the following observations using Einstein's photoelectric equation: (a) Photoelectric emission does not occur from a surface when the frequency of the light incident on it is less than a certain minimum value. (b) It is the frequency, and not the intensity of the incident light which affects the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons. (c) The cut-off voltage (V₀) versus frequency (ν) of the incident light curve is a straight line with a slope h/e.

key_points: (a) If hν < φ (work function), photon energy insufficient to liberate electron; threshold frequency ν₀ = φ/h
(b) KE_max = hν - φ; only frequency ν appears in this expression, not intensity; intensity only affects the number of photoelectrons
(c) eV₀ = hν - φ → V₀ = (h/e)ν - φ/e; slope of V₀ vs ν graph is h/e

questions.solution: Einstein's photoelectric equation: KE_max = hν - φ, where hν is the energy of one photon, φ is the work function of the metal, and KE_max is the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons. (a) For photoelectric emission to occur, the photon must have enough energy to overcome the work function: hν ≥ φ. If ν < φ/h = ν₀ (threshold frequency), no single photon has sufficient energy to eject an electron, so emission does not occur regardless of intensity. (b) KE_max = hν - φ depends only on the frequency ν of the incident light. Increasing intensity means more photons per second but each photon still has the same energy hν; thus more electrons are emitted but KE_max remains unchanged. (c) At the cut-off (stopping) potential V₀: eV₀ = hν - φ, so V₀ = (h/e)ν - φ/e. This is a linear equation in ν with slope h/e and intercept -φ/e, confirming that the V₀ vs ν graph is a straight line with slope h/e.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: (क) उन शर्तों का उल्लेख कीजिए जिनके अन्तर्गत दो संबद्ध स्रोतों से उत्पन्न दो प्रकाश तरंगें तरंगदैर्ध्य के पदों में (i) रचनात्मक रूप से, तथा (ii) विनाशात्मक रूप से एक-दूसरे के साथ व्यतिकरण कर सकती हैं। क्या इन शर्तों को दो सोडियम लैम्पों से उत्पन्न दो प्रकाशों के लिए अनुप्रयुक्त किया जा सकता है? कारण दीजिए। (ख) यंग के द्विझिरी प्रयोग में हरे रंग के एकवर्णी प्रकाश का उपयोग किया गया है तथा किसी परदे पर व्यतिकरण पैटर्न का प्रेक्षण किया गया है। यदि हरे प्रकाश को उसी तीव्रता के लाल एकवर्णी प्रकाश से प्रतिस्थापित कर दिया जाए, तो व्यतिकरण पैटर्न की फ्रिंज चौड़ाई किस प्रकार प्रभावित होगी? अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Write the conditions under which two light waves originating from two coherent sources can interfere each other (i) constructively, and (ii) destructively, in terms of wavelength. Can these be applied for two lights originating from two sodium lamps? Give reason. (b) Monochromatic light of green colour is used in Young's double slit experiment and an interference pattern is observed on a screen. If the green light is replaced by red monochromatic light of the same intensity, how will the fringe width of interference pattern be affected? Justify your answer.

key_points: Constructive: path difference = nλ (n = 0, 1, 2,...); Destructive: path difference = (2n-1)λ/2
Two sodium lamps cannot produce coherent light; each lamp emits light independently with random phase differences, so sustained interference is not possible
Red light has larger wavelength than green; fringe width β = λD/d increases when green is replaced by red

questions.solution: (a) For constructive interference: the path difference between two waves must be an integer multiple of the wavelength, i.e. Δx = nλ (where n = 0, 1, 2,...). For destructive interference: the path difference must be an odd multiple of half the wavelength, i.e. Δx = (2n - 1)λ/2. These conditions cannot be applied to two sodium lamps because the lamps emit light independently. The phase difference between their emissions is not constant and changes randomly with time, making them incoherent sources. Sustained interference requires coherent sources (constant phase relationship). (b) The fringe width is β = λD/d. Since red light has a longer wavelength than green light, and D and d remain the same, the fringe width will increase when green is replaced by red. The fringe pattern will be wider and more spread out.

questions.text: (क) (i) मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉनों के संख्या घनत्व तथा विश्रांति काल के पदों में किसी चालक की प्रतिरोधकता के लिए व्यंजन व्युत्पन्न कीजिए। (ii) आरेख में दो भिन्न समय अन्तरालों में किसी तार की अनुप्रस्थ-काट से प्रवाहित धारा का ग्राफ दर्शाया गया है। इन समय अन्तरालों में इस अनुप्रस्थ-काट से प्रवाहित आवेशों (Q₁ और Q₂) की तुलना कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) Derive an expression for the resistivity of a conductor in terms of number density of free electrons and relaxation time. (ii) The figure shows the plot of current through a cross-section of wire over two different time intervals. Compare the charges (Q₁ and Q₂) that pass through the cross-section during these time intervals.

key_points: Drift velocity vd = eEτ/m; J = nevd = ne²Eτ/m; E = ρJ → ρ = m/(ne²τ)
Charge Q = area under I-t graph
Q₁ = 2.0 × 2 = 4 C (rectangle), Q₂ = area of triangle = 0.5 × 4 × 2 = 4 C; Q₁ = Q₂

questions.solution: (a)(i) When an electric field E is applied across a conductor, electrons experience a force F = eE and acquire a drift velocity vd = eEτ/m, where τ is the relaxation time and m is the electron mass. The current density is J = nevd = ne²Eτ/m, where n is the number density of free electrons. Using Ohm's law J = E/ρ (where ρ is resistivity), we get ρ = E/J = m/(ne²τ). This is the required expression. (ii) The charge passing through the cross-section equals the area under the I-t graph. For Q₁ (rectangular region): Q₁ = 2·0 A × 2 s = 4 C. For Q₂ (triangular region): Q₂ = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 4 s × 2·0 A = 4 C. Therefore Q₁ = Q₂.

questions.text: (क) विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंगों के किन्हीं तीन अभिलक्षणों का उल्लेख कीजिए। (ख) किसी संधारित्र को आवेशित करते समय विस्थापन धारा का अस्तित्व कैसे और कहाँ होता है, संक्षेप में व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) State any three characteristics of electromagnetic waves. (b) Briefly explain how and where the displacement current exists during the charging of a capacitor.

key_points: EM wave characteristics: (i) transverse in nature — E and B are perpendicular to each other and to direction of propagation; (ii) travel at speed c = 3×10⁸ m/s in vacuum; (iii) carry energy and momentum; do not require material medium
During capacitor charging, a changing electric field exists between the plates
The displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) exists in the region between the capacitor plates where no conduction current flows

questions.solution: (a) Three characteristics of electromagnetic waves: (i) They are transverse waves — the electric field E and magnetic field B oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation. (ii) They travel through vacuum at the speed of light c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, and their speed is related to field amplitudes by E₀/B₀ = c. (iii) They carry energy and momentum and can exert radiation pressure; they do not require any material medium for propagation. (b) When a capacitor is being charged, conduction current flows in the external circuit but no actual charge flows between the plates. However, the electric field between the plates changes with time as charge builds up. This changing electric flux gives rise to the displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt), which exists in the space between the capacitor plates. Maxwell introduced this concept to make Ampere's circuital law consistent — the displacement current between the plates is equal in magnitude to the conduction current in the external wires.
questions.topic: Displacement Current and EM Wave Properties

questions.text: किसी हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में परमाणु के नाभिक पर स्थित प्रोटॉन के चारों ओर त्रिज्या r की वृत्ताकार कक्षा में कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन किसी निश्चित चाल v से परिक्रमा करता है। प्रोटॉन और परिक्रमी इलेक्ट्रॉन के बीच लगने वाला स्थिर-विद्युत आकर्षण बल इलेक्ट्रॉन को कक्षा में परिक्रमण करने के लिए आवश्यक अभिकेन्द्र बल प्रदान करता है। बोर मॉडल के अनुसार, एक इलेक्ट्रॉन निश्चित स्थायी कक्षाओं में ही परिक्रमण कर सकता है। इन कक्षाओं में इलेक्ट्रॉन का कोणीय संवेग h/2π का कोई पूर्णांक गुणज होता है, जहाँ h प्लांक स्थिरांक है। साथ ही, जब कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन उच्च ऊर्जा की कक्षा से निम्न ऊर्जा की कक्षा में संक्रमण करता है, तो कोई फ़ोटॉन उत्सर्जित होता है जिसकी ऊर्जा अंतिम अवस्था से प्रारम्भिक अवस्था की ऊर्जाओं के बीच अन्तर के बराबर होती है। यह मानते हुए कि इलेक्ट्रॉन का द्रव्यमान तथा आवेश क्रमश: m और e हैं, निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.text_english: A hydrogen atom consists of an electron revolving in a circular orbit of radius r with certain velocity v around a proton located at the nucleus of the atom. The electrostatic force of attraction between the revolving electron and the proton provides the requisite centripetal force to keep it in the orbit. According to Bohr's model, an electron can revolve only in certain stable orbits. The angular momentum of the electron in these orbits is some integral multiple of h/2π, where h is the Planck's constant. Further, when an electron makes a transition from one orbit of higher energy to that of lower energy, a photon is emitted having energy equal to the difference between energies of the initial and final states. Assuming the mass and charge of an electron as m and e respectively, answer the following questions.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 29 तथा 30 केस अध्ययन-आधारित प्रश्न हैं। निम्नलिखित अनुच्छेदों को पढ़ कर नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Questions number 29 and 30 are Case Study-based questions. Read the following paragraphs and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: कक्षा की त्रिज्या (r) तथा भौतिक नियतांक (K = 1/4πε₀) के पदों में इलेक्ट्रॉन की चाल v के लिए व्यंजक है:
sub_questions.text_english: The expression for the speed of electron v in terms of radius of the orbit (r) and physical constant (K = 1/4πε₀) is:
sub_questions.solution: The Coulomb force provides the centripetal force: Ke²/r² = mv²/r. Solving for v: v² = Ke²/(mr), so v = √(Ke²/mr). Option (C) is correct.

sub_questions.text: r और भौतिक नियतांक K के पदों में परमाणु की कुल ऊर्जा है:
sub_questions.text_english: The total energy of the atom in terms of r and physical constant K is:
sub_questions.solution: KE = mv²/2 = Ke²/2r (from centripetal condition). PE = -Ke²/r. Total energy E = KE + PE = Ke²/2r - Ke²/r = -Ke²/2r. The negative sign indicates a bound state. Option (B) is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी परमाणु में जब कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन एक अवस्था से दूसरी अवस्था में संक्रमण करता है, तो 500 nm तरंगदैर्ध्य का कोई फ़ोटॉन उत्सर्जित होता है। तब बोर मॉडल के अनुसार eV में इलेक्ट्रॉन की कुल ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन तथा इलेक्ट्रॉन की गतिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन क्रमश: होंगे:
sub_questions.text_english: A photon of wavelength 500 nm is emitted when an electron makes a transition from one state to the other state in an atom. The change in the total energy of the electron and change in its kinetic energy in eV as per Bohr's model, respectively will be:
sub_questions.solution: Photon energy = hc/λ = (6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸)/(500×10⁻⁹) = 3.978×10⁻¹⁹ J ≈ 2.48 eV. When a photon is emitted, the electron moves to a lower energy state. The total energy decreases by 2.48 eV (ΔE_total = -2.48 eV). In Bohr's model, KE = -E_total, so if total energy decreases by 2.48 eV, KE increases by +2.48 eV. Therefore the changes are –2·48 eV and +2·48 eV respectively. Option (C) is correct.

sub_questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में इलेक्ट्रॉन की nवीं कक्षा में परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति निम्नलिखित में से किसके आनुपातिक होती है?
sub_questions.text_english: In Bohr's model of hydrogen atom, the frequency of revolution of electron in its nth orbit is proportional to:
sub_questions.solution: The frequency of revolution f = v/(2πr). In Bohr's model, v ∝ 1/n and r ∝ n². Therefore f ∝ (1/n)/(n²) = 1/n³. Option (D) is correct.

questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र में दो चालक पट्टिकाएँ होती हैं जो सामान्यत: किसी दूरी पर एक-दूसरे के समान्तर रखी होती हैं। जब किसी संधारित्र को आवेशित किया जाता है, तो आवेश पट्टिकाओं के भीतरी पृष्ठों पर स्थित हो जाता है तथा पट्टिकाओं के बीच कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र स्थापित हो जाता है। इस प्रकार संधारित्र में स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा संचित होती है। आरेख में तीन धातु की बृहत वर्गाकार पट्टिकाएँ हैं जिनमें प्रत्येक की भुजा की लम्बाई 'L' है तथा ये एक-दूसरे के समान्तर और समदूरस्थ रखी हैं। P₁ और P₂ तथा P₂ और P₃ के रिक्त स्थान को परावैद्युतांक 'K' की अभ्रक की शीटों से पूर्णरूपेण भर दिया गया है। पट्टिका P₂ को बिन्दु A तथा अन्य पट्टिकाओं P₁ और P₃ को बिन्दु B से संयोजित किया गया है। बिन्दु B के सापेक्ष बिन्दु A के विभव को किसी धनात्मक विभव पर पोषित किया गया है तथा A और B के बीच विभवान्तर V है।
questions.text_english: A parallel plate capacitor consists of two conducting plates kept generally parallel to each other at a distance. When the capacitor is charged, the charge resides on the inner surfaces of the plates and an electric field is set up between them. Thus, electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor. The figure shows three large square metallic plates, each of side 'L' held parallel and equidistant from each other. The space between P₁ and P₂ and P₂ and P₃ is completely filled with mica sheets of dielectric constant 'K'. The plate P₂ is connected to point A and other plates P₁ and P₃ are connected to point B. Point A is maintained at a positive potential with respect to point B and the potential difference between A and B is V.

sub_questions.text: A और B के बीच निकाय की धारिता होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: The capacitance of the system between A and B will be:
sub_questions.solution: The arrangement consists of two capacitors: one between P₁ and P₂ (with dielectric K, area L², separation d) and one between P₂ and P₃ (same parameters). Each has capacitance C₀ = ε₀KL²/d. Since P₂ is connected to A and both P₁ and P₃ are connected to B, the two capacitors are in parallel. Total capacitance = 2C₀ = 2ε₀KL²/d. Option (C) is correct.

sub_questions.text_english: The charge on plate P₁ is:
sub_questions.solution: Each individual capacitor (e.g. between P₁ and P₂) has capacitance C₀ = ε₀KL²/d and is connected across potential difference V. Charge on plate P₁ = C₀ × V = (ε₀KL²/d) × V = ε₀VKL²/d. Wait — since A is at higher potential and P₂ is at A, P₁ is at B (lower potential). The charge on P₁ (which is the negative plate) is Q = C₀V = ε₀KL²V/d. But since there are two capacitors in parallel and the question asks only about P₁, the answer is ε₀VKL²/2d only if we consider half... Actually Q on P₁ = ε₀KL²/d × V = ε₀VKL²/d. The correct answer is (B) based on capacitance C₀V. Let me reconsider: each capacitor has C₀ = ε₀KL²/d and charge = C₀V = ε₀KL²V/d. Option (B) is correct.

sub_questions.text: P₁ और P₂ के बीच के प्रदेश में विद्युत-क्षेत्र है:
sub_questions.text_english: The electric field in the region between P₁ and P₂ is:
sub_questions.solution: The potential difference between P₁ and P₂ is V (since P₂ is at potential V with respect to P₁ which is at B = 0). The electric field between parallel plates is E = V/d (where d is the separation between P₁ and P₂). Therefore the electric field is V/d. Option (A) is correct.

sub_questions.text: इस निकाय के समान धारिता वाले वायु से भरे समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र, जिसकी पट्टिकाओं का क्षेत्रफल (L²) समान है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन होगा:
sub_questions.text_english: The separation between the plates of same area (L²) of a parallel plate air capacitor having capacitance equal to that of this system, will be:
sub_questions.solution: The system capacitance is C_sys = 2ε₀KL²/d. For an air capacitor of area L² and separation d', C_air = ε₀L²/d'. Setting C_air = C_sys: ε₀L²/d' = 2ε₀KL²/d → d' = d/(2K). Option (C) is correct.

questions.text: (क) (i) कोई बिम्ब 10 cm फोकस दूरी के किसी पतले उत्तल लेंस से 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। यह लेंस परदे पर तीक्ष्ण प्रतिबिम्ब बनाता है। यदि किसी पतले अवतल लेंस को उत्तल लेंस के सम्पर्क में रख दिया जाए, तो परदे पर तीक्ष्ण प्रतिबिम्ब बनता है जब परदे को अपनी आरम्भिक स्थिति से 45 cm विस्थापित किया जाता है। अवतल लेंस की फोकस दूरी परिकलित कीजिए। (ii) किसी समबाहु प्रिज्म का न्यूनतम विचलन कोण परिकलित कीजिए। प्रिज्म का अपवर्तनांक √3 है। न्यूनतम विचलन के इस प्रकरण के लिए आपतन कोण भी परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) An object is placed 30 cm from a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The lens forms a sharp image on a screen. If a thin concave lens is placed in contact with the convex lens, the sharp image on the screen is formed when the screen is moved by 45 cm from its initial position. Calculate the focal length of the concave lens. (ii) Calculate the angle of minimum deviation of an equilateral prism. The refractive index of the prism is √3. Calculate the angle of incidence for this case of minimum deviation also.

key_points: Part (i): Using lens formula for convex lens alone: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f → image at 15 cm; with concave lens, new image at 15+45=60 cm; using combined lens formula gives f_concave = -30 cm
Part (ii): For equilateral prism A = 60°; μ = sin((A + δ_min)/2)/sin(A/2); √3 = sin((60°+δ_min)/2)/sin30° → sin((60°+δ_min)/2) = √3/2 → (60°+δ_min)/2 = 60° → δ_min = 60°
Angle of incidence at minimum deviation: i = (A + δ_min)/2 = (60+60)/2 = 60°

questions.solution: (a)(i) For the convex lens alone: u = -30 cm, f = +10 cm. Using 1/v - 1/u = 1/f: 1/v - 1/(-30) = 1/10 → 1/v = 1/10 - 1/30 = 2/30 → v = +15 cm. The image is formed 15 cm to the right of the lens. When the concave lens is placed in contact, the screen must be moved 45 cm further, so the new image is at v' = 15 + 45 = 60 cm from the lens combination. Using the lens formula for the combination: 1/v' - 1/u = 1/F → 1/60 - 1/(-30) = 1/F → 1/F = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20 → F = 20 cm. Using 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂: 1/20 = 1/10 + 1/f₂ → 1/f₂ = 1/20 - 1/10 = -1/20 → f₂ = -20 cm. The focal length of the concave lens is -20 cm. (ii) For the equilateral prism, A = 60°. Using the prism formula: μ = sin((A + δ_min)/2)/sin(A/2). √3 = sin((60° + δ_min)/2)/sin(30°) = sin((60° + δ_min)/2)/0·5. So sin((60° + δ_min)/2) = √3/2 = sin60°. Therefore (60° + δ_min)/2 = 60°, giving δ_min = 60°. The angle of incidence at minimum deviation is i = (A + δ_min)/2 = (60° + 60°)/2 = 60°.

questions.text: (क) (i) दो बिन्दु आवेश +q और –q, x-y तल में (a, 0) तथा (–a, 0) पर रखे हैं। इन आवेशों के कारण बिन्दु (0, y) पर नेट विद्युत-क्षेत्र के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए। इस प्रकार किसी दूरस्थ बिन्दु (y >> a) पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र ज्ञात कीजिए। (ii) भुजा 0·2 m के किसी समबाहु त्रिभुज के तीन शीर्षों A, B और C पर –2 nC, –1 nC और +5 nC के तीन बिन्दु आवेश स्थित हैं। आवेशों को A से A₁, B से B₁ तथा C से C₁ तक विस्थापित करने में किया गया कुल कार्य ज्ञात कीजिए। यहाँ A₁, B₁ और C₁ क्रमश: भुजा AB, BC और CA के मध्य-बिन्दु हैं।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) Two point charges + q and –q are held at (a, 0) and (–a, 0) in x-y plane. Obtain an expression for the net electric field due to the charges at a point (0, y). Hence, find electric field at a far off point (y >> a). (ii) Three point charges of –2 nC, –1 nC, and +5 nC are kept at the vertices A, B and C of an equilateral triangle of side 0·2 m. Find the total amount of work done in shifting the charges from A to A₁, B to B₁ and C to C₁. Here A₁, B₁ and C₁ are the midpoints of sides AB, BC and CA, respectively.

key_points: E at (0,y): each charge is at distance r = √(a²+y²); components along y cancel; net E = 2Kqa/(a²+y²)^(3/2) along negative x-axis (–x direction for dipole)
For y >> a: E ≈ 2Kqa/y³ = Kp/y³ where p = 2qa is the dipole moment
Work done = W = ΔPE = U_final - U_initial; calculate initial and final potential energies

questions.solution: (a)(i) Each charge (+q at (a,0) and –q at (–a,0)) is at a distance r = √(a² + y²) from point (0, y). The electric field due to +q points away from +q (toward (0,y) direction), and due to –q points toward –q. The y-components of the fields from both charges cancel each other. The x-components both point in the negative x-direction and add. Net E = 2 × (Kq/(a²+y²)) × (a/√(a²+y²)) = 2Kqa/(a²+y²)^(3/2), directed along the negative x-axis (along the dipole axis from +q to –q). For y >> a: E ≈ 2Kqa/y³ = K(2qa)/y³ = Kp/y³, where p = 2qa is the electric dipole moment. (ii) Side of triangle a = 0·2 m. The midpoints A₁, B₁, C₁ are all at distance 0·1 m from each other (side = 0·1 m for the inner triangle). Initial potential energy U_i = K[q_Aq_B/r_AB + q_Bq_C/r_BC + q_Aq_C/r_AC] = 9×10⁹ × [(-2×10⁻⁹)(-1×10⁻⁹)/0.2 + (-1×10⁻⁹)(5×10⁻⁹)/0.2 + (-2×10⁻⁹)(5×10⁻⁹)/0.2] = 9×10⁹ × [10⁻¹⁸(2-5-10)/0.2] = 9×10⁹ × (-13×10⁻¹⁸/0.2) = -585×10⁻⁹ J. Final U_f with side 0·1 m: U_f = 9×10⁹ × (-13×10⁻¹⁸/0.1) = -1170×10⁻⁹ J. Work done W = U_f - U_i = -1170×10⁻⁹ + 585×10⁻⁹ = -585×10⁻⁹ J = -585 nJ ≈ -5.85×10⁻⁷ J.

questions.text: (क) (i) लेंज़ का नियम लिखिए और व्याख्या कीजिए कि यह नियम किस प्रकार ऊर्जा संरक्षण नियम का कोई परिणाम है। (ii) भुजा l/2 का कोई वर्गाकार पाश आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार आरम्भ में किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B सदिश के बाहर है। इस पाश को किसी नियत वेग v सदिश से दाईं ओर तब तक ले जाया जाता है जब तक यह चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के प्रदेश से बाहर नहीं हो जाता है। (I) पाश के क्षेत्र में प्रवेश करते समय तथा पाश के क्षेत्र से बाहर आने पर इसमें प्रेरित धारा की दिशाएँ क्या होंगी? (II) समय t के साथ पाश से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स φ के विचरण तथा समय t के साथ पाश में प्रेरित वि.वा. बल (emf) E के विचरण के ग्राफ खींचिए। इन ग्राफों पर E, φ तथा t के सुसंगत मान अंकित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) State Lenz's law and explain how this law is a consequence of conservation of energy principle. (ii) A square shaped loop of side l/2 is initially lying outside a region of uniform magnetic field B (vector) as shown in the figure. The loop is moved towards right with a constant velocity v (vector) till it goes out of the region of magnetic field. (I) What will be the directions of induced current when the loop enters the field and when it leaves the field? (II) Draw the plots showing the variation of magnetic flux φ linked with the loop with time t and variation of induced emf E with time t. Mark the relevant values of E, φ and t on the graphs.

key_points: Lenz's law: induced current opposes the change causing it; this ensures energy conservation as work done by external agent equals electrical energy generated
Entering: flux increases (into page), so induced current opposes increase → induced current flows anticlockwise (counterclockwise) to create flux out of page
Leaving: flux decreases, induced current flows clockwise to maintain flux into page

questions.solution: (a)(i) Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced current in a conductor is such that the magnetic field created by the induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it. This is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy. If the induced current were to aid the change in flux, it would reinforce the motion causing it, producing more current, which would produce more motion — a perpetual motion scenario that violates energy conservation. Instead, the induced current creates a retarding force, requiring an external agent to do work. This work is converted into electrical energy in the circuit, consistent with energy conservation. (ii)(I) When the loop enters the magnetic field (directed into the page), the flux through the loop increases. By Lenz's law, the induced current must oppose this increase by creating a magnetic field out of the page inside the loop. Using the right-hand rule, this means the induced current flows anticlockwise (counterclockwise) when viewed from the front. When the loop exits the field, the flux decreases. The induced current must oppose this decrease by creating a field into the page, so it flows clockwise. (II) The flux-time graph shows: φ = 0 before entry; φ increases linearly from 0 to B(l/2)² = Bl²/4 as the loop enters (over time t₁ = (l/2)/v = l/2v); φ remains constant at Bl²/4 while the loop is fully inside; then decreases linearly back to zero as the loop exits. The emf-time graph shows: E = 0 before entry; E = B(l/2)v = Blv/2 (constant) while entering; E = 0 when fully inside; E = -Blv/2 (constant, opposite sign) while exiting.
